title: Implementing support for Interactive and AI workloads in a traditional HPC environment
problem: Interactive and AI workloads conflict with batch HPC jobs in traditional scheduling; incompatible QoS requirements
motivation: HPC centers need to support diverse workload types; interactive jobs suffer high queue times
method: Slurm divides all work into short time periods instead of letting any single job run to completion, cycling through different tasks rapidly. Interactive and AI workloads receive high priority and guaranteed resource allocations (specific portions of the computer reserved exclusively for them), ensuring they get quick response times, while batch jobs run during the unused capacity in between.
key_novelty: The approach reserves dedicated computing resources with high priority for interactive and AI work, allowing these responsive workloads to coexist with traditional batch jobs on the same scheduling system without conflicting demands.
